title: Finite degree-zero and vanishing positive cohomology of the dense-open boundary
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a reduced curve [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and $F$ a constructible etale sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense open. Give its closed complement the reduced induced scheme structure, defined by the radical ideal of functions vanishing there, and write $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ for this closed immersion. Let $B=i_*i^{-1}F$, with direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. For the underlying abelian sheaf $B_{\mathrm{ab}}$, the group $H^0(X,B_{\mathrm{ab}})$ is finite and $H^q(X,B_{\mathrm{ab}})=0$ for every $q>0$, where cohomology is [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. No prime annihilator or properness is assumed, and the empty complement is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), proof, closed complement and finite stalk product; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GJA

proof.text: Apply exists_dense_irreducible_opens to shrink U to a dense finite union W with zero-dimensional complement. The closed-complement immersion identifies Z with a subspace of X minus U, hence with a subspace of X minus W. The inducing-map Krull dimension inequality gives dim Z <= 0. Closed immersion composed with f is separated and finite type, so the zero-dimensional cohomology theorem applies, including empty X and empty Z.

Pullback preserves constructibility, so G=i^*F is constructible. The proved upstream tool Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf.isFiniteSheaf gives finitely generated geometric stalks. ModuleCat.isFinitelyGenerated_iff and Module.finite_of_finite give finite underlying sets over finite Lambda. Point.sheafFiberCompIso commutes the stalk with forgetful passage to abelian groups. Thus every abelian stalk of G is finite.

Apply zero_dimensional_etale_cohomology to Z, i composed with f, the underlying abelian sheaf A of G, and the algebraic-closure geometric point at each z. Its index set Z is finite. Inject the categorical product of its finite stalks into the dependent function type using its projections; Concrete.isLimit_ext proves injectivity. The degree-zero map in the theorem is an isomorphism. Compose it with nonempty_sheafH_extDerivedIso to inject Sheaf.H A 0 into that finite product. In every positive degree the same Ext-to-derived isomorphism transfers the subsingleton conclusion to Sheaf.H A q.

Forgetting module structure commutes definitionally with closed-immersion direct image. Use bijective_edgeMap_of_isFinite for i and A in each degree: injectivity transfers finite degree-zero cohomology and subsingleton positive-degree cohomology from Z to X. This proves the two original conclusions, with every signature unchanged.

lean.statement: theorem dense_open_boundary_cohomology (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ] {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve f] [IsReduced X] (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) [Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf F] (U : X.Opens) (hU : Dense (U : Set X)) : let I := Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal U.compl let B := (I.subschemeι)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ].obj ((I.subschemeι)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ].obj F) let B' := (sheafCompose X.smallEtaleTopology (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).obj B Finite (Sheaf.H B' 0) ∧ (∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → Subsingleton (Sheaf.H B' q))
